item.title: 3 prisoners die at DMCH within 1 hour 40 minutes
item.description:
Three prisoners receiving treatment at Dhaka Medical College Hospital (DMCH) after falling ill at Dhaka Central Jail in Keraniganj died at separate times today, Sunday. 

Two of them were undertrial prisoners, while the third was a convicted prisoner. The two undertrial prisoners died 1 hour and 40 minutes apart.

The deceased have been identified as Abul Bashar, 58; Abdul Qayyum, 62; and Md Shahadat Hossain Liton, 52.

According to hospital sources, several prison guards, including Md Shahid, brought Abul Bashar to the emergency department of DMCH this morning after he fell ill. Following examination, the attending physician declared him dead at 7:25 am.

Abul Bashar was from Kutia Lakshmipur village in Kachua upazila of Chandpur. His father’s name was Sekendar Ali. He had been detained in connection with a case filed under the Women and Children Repression Prevention Act at Kachua police station.

Another undertrial prisoner, Abdul Qayyum, was brought to the hospital’s emergency department in the morning by several prison guards, including Hemayet Hossain, on the instructions of the prison authorities. After examination, the physician declared him dead at 9:05 am.

Qayyum was from Golai Padabazar village in Chauddagram upazila of Cumilla. He had been detained in connection with eight cases.

Meanwhile, convicted prisoner Shahadat Hossain Liton was admitted to Ward 502 of the Medicine Department at Dhaka Medical College Hospital on 28 August after falling ill. He was undergoing treatment there when the attending physician declared him dead at around 8:45 am today.

He had been detained in connection with Speedy Trial Tribunal Case No. 11/07 and a case filed at Uttara police station under Sections 302, 34 and 201 of the Penal Code, Case No. 9(11)06.

Liton was from Pabla village at Daulatpur in Khulna.

Md Habibur Rahman, inspector at the Dhaka Medical College Hospital police outpost, said the bodies of all three prisoners had been kept at the hospital morgue for post-mortem examinations.

item.title: Mustafizur’s 10 best career moments, on his 31st birthday
item.description:
Happy birthday, Mustafizur Rahman. One of Bangladesh’s greatest-ever pace bowlers turns 31 today. He has been playing international cricket for 11 years, and his career is filled with memorable moments. On his birthday, here are the 10 best moments of Mustafizur’s career.

It started with Afridi

24 April, 2015. Mustafizur’s first day in international cricket. The opponent was Pakistan. But this was the Pakistan of Shahid Afridi—‘Boom Boom’ was still a formidable force. And Mustafizur started with him.

Afridi became Mustafizur’s first international wicket. He later dismissed Mohammad Hafeez as well. He finished with two wickets for 20 runs in four overs. Sixteen of his 24 deliveries were dot balls. Bangladesh beat Pakistan after 16 years.

Dhoni’s collision and Mustafizur’s response

Just two months after making his T20 debut, Mustafizur made his ODI debut on 18 June, 2015. He immediately made an impression, dismissing Rohit Sharma and Ajinkya Rahane. But because of his inexperience, he repeatedly stopped in the middle of his run-up. Rohit brought it to the umpire’s attention. Dhoni, without saying anything, walked straight into him.

The collision forced Mustafizur to leave the field for medical attention. After returning, he dismissed Suresh Raina, Ravichandran Ashwin and Ravindra Jadeja. He finished his debut with five wickets for 50 runs, was named Player of the Match, and Bangladesh won.

Dismantling India

Five wickets in the first match, six in the second. Eleven wickets in two games. He added another two in the third ODI. With 13 wickets in his first-ever series, Mustafizur was named Player of the Series.

His ability to trouble India’s star-studded batting lineup instantly made him the centre of attention.

A sensation in Test cricket too

Mustafizur went wicketless in his first 13 overs of his Test debut. It seemed he might have been brought into the format too soon. But magic arrived in the 14th over.

He dismissed Hashim Amla with the first ball and JP Duminy with the next. He missed out on a hat-trick but bowled Quinton de Kock with the fourth delivery. Three wickets in one over.

The match was drawn due to rain, but Mustafizur was named Player of the Match.

Cutter magic on the world stage

At the 2016 T20 World Cup, Mustafizur took five wickets for 22 runs against New Zealand. Four of his victims, including Kane Williamson, were bowled.

He took nine wickets in three matches. After wreaking havoc with his cutters in the series against India, the ‘Cutter Master’ continued to shine at the World Cup. That performance helped earn him an opportunity in the IPL.

First IPL victims: de Villiers and Watson

In his first IPL match, Mustafizur’s first victims were AB de Villiers and Shane Watson. Playing for Sunrisers Hyderabad, he took two wickets for 26 runs in four overs.

The other five bowlers in the team conceded more than 12 runs per over, while Mustafizur’s economy rate was just 6.50.

The yorker that floored Russell

The image remains vivid in cricket fans’ memories. Shakib Al Hasan was playing for Kolkata, while Mustafizur represented Hyderabad. A brilliant yorker from Mustafizur not only bowled Kolkata’s Andre Russell but also sent him tumbling onto the stumps.

That was the only real moment of excitement in the entire match.

The heart and soul of Hyderabad


Mustafizur played a role in every Sunrisers Hyderabad victory that season. He took 17 wickets in 16 matches at an average of 24.76, with an economy rate of just 6.90.

It was not just about the numbers. He played a role at key turning points in the team’s successful campaign. As a result, he became the first overseas player to win the IPL’s Emerging Player award. To this day, he remains the only overseas player to have received the honour.

20 wickets in his first World Cup

His ODI World Cup debut was equally impressive. At the 2019 World Cup, he took 20 wickets in eight matches. He claimed five wickets against India and another five against Pakistan.

He finished the tournament as the fourth-highest wicket-taker.

A new Bangladesh record

In 2024, Mustafizur made history against the United States in Houston. No Bangladeshi bowler had previously taken six wickets in an international T20.

He took six wickets for just 10 runs in four overs. Mustafizur also holds the record for the most wickets by a Bangladeshi bowler in T20 internationals.

item.title: Joining Mecca pact could undermine our security and trade interests
item.description:
Prothom Alo recently interviewed M Humayun Kabir, president of the non-government research institute Bangladesh Enterprise Institute (BEI) and former diplomat and ambassador, in the wake of diverse discussions surrounding the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement. The interview was conducted by Sohul Ahmed.

What global realities have influenced the signing of the 'Mecca Joint Defence Agreement'?

M Humayun Kabir: The geopolitical context of the Mecca Agreement can primarily be divided into two main parts. The immediate cause is the current Iran crisis and the 'security vacuum' created by the activities of the United States and Israel in the Middle East.

After the Iranian revolution, an undeclared strategic security ring, led by the US and Israel and incorporating Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Kuwait, Jordan, and the United Arab Emirates, was formed to exert pressure on Iran in the Middle East. Its aim was to shield other Middle Eastern countries from the revolution's impact.

The recent attacks on American bases during the Iran war have created uncertainty around conventional security, prompting US allies to seek alternative measures. As a new security initiative, Saudi Arabia signed a major defence agreement with Pakistan in September 2025. Meanwhile, NATO member Turkey, under the continuous threat from Israel, is unable to fully trust NATO, prompting them to consider joining a new defence framework.

The dominance of the Petrodollar, the US's unconditional support for Israel, atrocities in Gaza, and agreements like the Abraham Accords have fundamentally altered the equation in the Middle East. This changing situation and the consideration of how to fill the void if the US reduces its strength in the Middle East led to the emergence of the Mecca Agreement.

However, the Mecca Agreement is not yet a complete system; it is a 'partial security framework'. In short, the Mecca Agreement has been accelerated to counter Iran's growing influence and consolidate its participants in the face of the US's uncertain role.

Bangladesh maintains close ties with both China and the United States. Will the Mecca Agreement complicate our international relations?

M Humayun Kabir: It's difficult to say for sure. In recent times, China's diplomatic position has been particularly significant. During the Iran crisis, we saw China primarily siding with Iran. Also, in 2023, China played a crucial role in establishing a historic understanding between Saudi Arabia and Iran.

China, like the US, would not favour any political instability, division, or conflict in Bangladesh that might counter its business interests. Similarly, the US also desires long-term stability in Bangladesh. A peaceful environment in Bangladesh that allows for unhindered business development would safeguard both economic welfare for the general public and US commercial interests.

Overall, analysis suggests that both China and the US, as major powers, are likely to support maintaining Bangladesh's current balanced foreign policy approach.

Why has the Mecca Agreement become significant for Bangladesh?

M Humayun Kabir: Two perspectives primarily drive the interest in this agreement in Bangladesh. First, since it is the 'Mecca Agreement,' there is a tendency to associate it with a religious interpretation and sentiment. The argument is that being part of such an alliance will enhance internal cohesion among Muslim countries and strengthen national security.

Second, in many discussions, the current strained relationship between Bangladesh and India and regional security are significant. Given India's status as a large neighbour and existing diplomatic tensions, many harbour security-related concerns. Joining such a defence alliance is seen by many as a way to better manage potential security risks or concerns.

How do you perceive Bangladesh's positive attitude toward joining a defence alliance for the first time?

M Humayun Kabir: Since Bangladesh's independence, we have never participated in any military alliance. Even without explicit UN approval, we have never engaged in international military or peacekeeping missions. Despite various political changes over time, Bangladesh has never deviated from its neutral foreign policy. Joining such a military alliance would be a fundamental change to our long-established security and diplomatic framework, requiring considerable prudence and caution.

Secondly, the current government's declared foreign policy emphasises 'Bangladesh First'. The foundation of this policy is to maintain balanced relations with all, ensuring national interests without leaning toward any particular power. If Bangladesh joins this new military alliance, it could call the government's neutral stance into question. Therefore, before making a final decision, it is crucial to thoroughly analyse the alignment of this with our long-standing national consensus and the current government's own foreign policy.

What are the potential risks and benefits of joining this alliance?

M Humayun Kabir: When discussing the possible benefits of this agreement, the foremost considerations are military and technological cooperation. Additionally, there is the prospect of financial assistance from Saudi Arabia and increased benefits for our massive labour market in the Middle East.

However, the risks are equally significant. First, the Middle East has been an extreme conflict zone for decades, and Bangladesh has historically remained outside it. Joining this alliance increases the risk of becoming directly involved in Middle Eastern conflicts.

Secondly, if this alliance is viewed as a 'Sunni alliance', Bangladesh's existing friendly relations with countries of other sects may face challenges.

Thirdly, there could be a negative impact on our foreign trade. The primary route for Bangladesh's garment exports is the Bab-el-Mandeb Strait in the Red Sea, currently influenced by Yemen's Houthis, with ongoing conflict with Saudi Arabia. Directly joining this alliance could make Bangladesh a target for the Houthis.

The crucial aspect is that we currently maintain successful bilateral military and diplomatic relations with Turkey, Saudi Arabia, and Pakistan. The benefits we enjoy bilaterally can be maintained without joining this agreement, with no risk involved. Therefore, we must consider whether to stay risk-free through bilateral relations or join an alliance and face new challenges.

There seems to be a strong reaction from India regarding Bangladesh's potential involvement in this agreement. How should Bangladesh view India's concerns?

M Humayun Kabir: India's behaviour or reaction is their own concern. Our decisions should be made entirely based on our national interests. Although the discussions of this agreement are currently limited to security, one of the main pillars of national interest is economic prosperity. Our economy is closely tied to China, India, the United States, the European Union, and Southeast Asian countries; maintaining this balance is crucial for us.

What should be the process for making a decision regarding joining any defence alliance?

M Humayun Kabir: For such significant decisions, the necessity of a discussion in the national parliament is undeniable. Outside of parliament, it's also important to have detailed discussions with civil society, the media, various research institutes, and experienced diplomats. This should not merely be an internal government decision; instead, an open and transparent process involving input from all stakeholders is necessary.

Thank you.

M Humayun Kabir: Thank you.

item.title: Who will become Argentina’s captain after Messi’s retirement?
item.description:
Who will be Argentina’s new captain? Lionel Messi’s retirement has brought a major chapter in Argentine football to an end. Messi had been the Albiceleste’s captain for more than 15 years. Under his leadership, Argentina achieved a series of major successes, including winning the World Cup. Now, who will wear the armband?

Three contenders for the captaincy

Cristian Romero appears to be the leading candidate to succeed Messi. The 27-year-old defender is one of the most important players in Lionel Scaloni’s Argentina side. He has long been a dependable presence in Argentina’s defence. He also has leadership experience at English club Tottenham. His presence on the pitch gives his teammates confidence.

Following Nicolas Otamendi’s departure from the national team, Romero has become one of the most experienced defenders in the squad.

Spanish newspaper AS reported that Romero is the frontrunner for the captaincy. Argentine radio station Radio Mitre reported that the Argentine Football Association (AFA) has already chosen Romero as its preferred candidate. However, no official announcement has been made.

The biggest challenger to Romero could be Emiliano Martinez. The goalkeeper has played a major role in Argentina’s recent success. He won the Best Goalkeeper award at the 2022 World Cup in Qatar.

Although Martinez could not produce his best form at the 2026 World Cup, he performed well in the final. He has joined Chelsea this season and is renowned for his ability to save penalties. He is also adept at psychological battles and knows how to stand up for his teammates and lead from the front.

Another Martinez who could be in contention is Lautaro Martinez. The forward has been Inter Milan’s captain for several seasons. His goalscoring ability has also made him one of the club’s biggest stars. Just yesterday, he scored twice against Napoli to help Inter Milan secure a victory. Lautaro was part of almost the entire Scaloni era alongside Messi. He is therefore no stranger to the demands of leadership within the national team.

Scaloni’s future also matters

Scaloni, who will play a major role in deciding the next captain, is another factor to consider. Following the World Cup final, Scaloni himself said he would continue until December and then speak with the association president. He also said he wanted to take some time to rest. For now, however, he will be the one to announce the preliminary squad for Argentina’s upcoming international friendlies.

Argentina are preparing to play three matches at home during the September international window. The games could take place between 21 September and 6 October, although the opponents have yet to be finalised.

The answer to the question of who will become Argentina’s new captain is likely to emerge when the squad for those matches is announced.

item.title: Activities of some accused suspicious, there could be sabotage: Chief Prosecutor
item.description:
Chief Prosecutor of the International Crimes Tribunal (ICT) Md Aminul Islam has said security personnel have been alerted to step up security at the tribunal, citing concerns over the suspicious movements and activities of some of the accused.

“There are some accused whose movements and activities have appeared suspicious. We have received some confidential information suggesting that some of them may carry out acts of sabotage or other disruptive activities,” he said.

The chief prosecutor made the remarks at a briefing at his office at the ICT on Sunday.

Responding to a journalist’s question, Aminul Islam said security personnel had been alerted to strengthen security at the tribunal. He said the movements and activities of some of the accused had appeared suspicious and that the prosecution had received confidential information indicating that some of them might carry out acts of sabotage or other disruptive activities.

He said the prosecution was assessing and analysing the situation and taking appropriate measures.

Aminul Islam also said a law titled “Enforced Disappearance Prevention and Redress Act” was in the process of being introduced, describing it as a highly timely piece of legislation.

He said the law could give fresh momentum to the prosecution of enforced disappearance cases across the country.

“Those involved in enforced disappearances are extremely powerful. Keeping that in mind, we ourselves are remaining vigilant,” he said.

He also urged family members of victims of enforced disappearance to remain cautious and called on the government to provide all-round cooperation on the matter.

Asked by a journalist why the word “sabotage” had been appearing more frequently in statements over the past week, the ICT chief prosecutor said every activity, both inside and outside the tribunal, was under their surveillance.

“That is why, if anyone attempts any subversive activity, it will be suicidal for them,” he said. “If anyone has such malicious thoughts, or if any offender is contemplating anything else, it will ultimately be self-destructive.”

The tribunal’s investigation agency is investigating alleged crimes against humanity based on complaints filed by Mayer Daak, an organisation representing families of victims of enforced disappearance.

Members of 55 families of victims of enforced disappearance visited the Office of the Chief Prosecutor at the tribunal on Sunday. The investigation agency is scheduled to record their statements. The family members were present during the chief prosecutor’s briefing.

Aminul Islam said that since investigations into the complaints lodged by these families began, the activities of some criminals had also increased.

“Law enforcement agencies must remain vigilant,” he said. “The administration needs to keep a close watch on those currently facing trial before the tribunal. Attention must also be given to every family of victims of enforced disappearance so that their security can be strengthened.”

“There is no reason to consider a criminal a friend,” the chief prosecutor said. “They may strike at any time, in their own way.”

He also urged the government to remain vigilant. He said the prosecution was advising families of victims of enforced disappearance to remain cautious, particularly to ensure that the ongoing investigations were not disrupted in any way.

“No one should be able to obstruct the investigation by carrying out sabotage or otherwise interfering with the proceedings,” he added.

item.title: TOP SHOTS (6 September 2026)
The world’s 10 most valuable squads
item.description:
SOCCER-SPAIN-ESP-RMA/

The value of football stars is measured not only by their performances on the pitch, but also by their market worth. Some players take to the field with price tags worth hundreds of millions of euros, while others keep driving their values higher with their performances. Following the close of the summer transfer window, Transfermarkt has recalculated those figures. The result shows that Real Madrid have reclaimed the throne as the world’s most valuable squad. Most of the other top clubs, meanwhile, are from the English Premier League.

Here is a look at the world’s 10 most valuable squads.

1. Real Madrid: €1.46 billion

According to Transfermarkt, Real Madrid currently have the world’s most valuable squad. With Kylian Mbappe, Vinicius Junior and Jude Bellingham driving the huge market value of their attack, the club also added several important players during the summer. The arrivals of players such as Yan Diomande, Marc Cucurella and Ibrahima Konate have further increased the squad’s overall market value. Real Madrid currently have 27 players, with an average value of more than €53.9 million per player.

2. Manchester City: €1.43 billion

Manchester City were at the top until recently. The English Premier League side have dropped to second following the summer transfer window. City strengthened their squad by bringing in midfielders such as Enzo Fernandez, Elliot Anderson and Ayoub Bouaddi. With a market value of €1.43 billion for a 25-man squad, they remain close behind Real Madrid.

3. PSG: €1.36 billion

Two-time defending Champions League winners PSG are third. Luis Enrique’s squad has five players with market values of €100 million or more. Stars such as Joao Neves, Vitinha, Ousmane Dembele, Desire Doue and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia have helped push the club’s total market value so high.

4. Arsenal: €1.33 billion

Arsenal and PSG have the smallest squads among the top 10, with 24 players each. The current Premier League champions have consistently strengthened their squad over the past few seasons. As their success on the pitch has grown, so too have their players’ market values. New additions such as Bruno Guimaraes and Ezequiel Calafiori have also increased the squad’s overall value. Arsenal are fourth with a total market value of €1.33 billion.

5. Barcelona: €1.26 billion

One of the world’s most valuable players belongs to Barcelona—Lamine Yamal (€220 million), the same valuation as City’s Haaland. According to Transfermarkt, Yamal’s market value stands at €220 million. Alongside Yamal, players such as Raphinha, Pedri and Pau Cubarsi have helped make Barcelona’s squad one of the most valuable in the world. The 27 players in Barcelona’s squad have an average value of €46.7 million.

6. Chelsea: €1.08 billion

Chelsea have the youngest squad by average age among the top 10 most valuable teams. Their 28-player squad has an average age of 24.4 years. The impact of Chelsea’s huge investments over the years is clearly reflected in their players’ market values. The English club are sixth with a squad worth €1.08 billion.

7. Bayern Munich: €1.04 billion

Bayern Munich have the most valuable squad in the Bundesliga. The German club’s total market value stands at €1.04 billion. Michael Olise is one of their most valuable players. Bayern are also the only German representative among Europe’s top clubs in this ranking.

8. Liverpool: €1.03 billion

Liverpool have moved up in terms of their players’ market values. They currently rank eighth with a squad worth €1.03 billion. The signing of Bradley Barcola late in the transfer window was the main reason behind the increase in the squad’s market value. Liverpool currently have 27 players in their squad.

9. Manchester United: €924.3 million

Manchester United ended the summer transfer window after making major changes to their midfield. They rank ninth with a squad market value of €924.3 million. United also have more players in their squad than most of the other teams in the top 10. The club have 30 players, with an average value of more than €30.8 million each.

10. Tottenham Hotspur: €824 million

Tottenham are the final team in the top 10. The north London club spent heavily during the summer transfer window, and that investment is reflected in the squad’s market value. Tottenham rank 10th with a total value of €824 million. Their 28-player squad has an average value of more than €29.4 million per player.

item.title: Haaland heads unconvincing Man City top of Premier League
item.description:
TOPSHOT-FBL-ENG-PR-MAN CITY-COVENTRY

Erling Haaland maintained Manchester City's perfect start to the Premier League season but Enzo Maresca's men were made to sweat for a 1-0 victory over newly-promoted Coventry at the Etihad on Saturday.

Maresca was able to unleash Enzo Fernandez and Iliman Ndiaye after their arrivals completed a record outlay by any club of £460 million ($622 million) in the transfer market to refresh the City squad after Pep Guardiola's decade in charge.

The Maresca era has started with three consecutive Premier League wins, but it was a far from perfect performance as the hosts needed a pair of late saves from Gianluigi Donnarumma to deny Coventry a first top-flight point for 25 years.

Haaland's header midway through the first half proved decisive for his third goal in as many games this season.

"Nine out of 10 times in this kind of game at the end you finish conceding," Maresca said. "But the way we suffered together until the end, defending throw-ins, set-pieces, was good. Not all wins are going to be nice wins."

Fernandez was supposed to start on the bench after completing his £125 million move from Chelsea to match the Premier League transfer record.
However, an injury to Nico O'Reilly in the warm-up meant the Argentine was thrust into the starting line-up.

Ndiaye was also handed his City debut by Maresca alongside Haaland, Antoine Semenyo and Rayan Cherki in a fearsome front four.

Coventry had failed to even score in three consecutive defeats to mark their return to the top flight after over two decades away.

Yet, Frank Lampard's men could not have come closer to breaking their duck early on thanks to a gift from Donnarumma.

The giant Italian mis-controlled a backpass and recovered to clear off his own line with inches to spare.

Taiwo Awoniyi and Jack Rudoni also missed big chances to give the visitors the lead before City began to find their stride.

Cherki smashed off the post before Fernandez was involved in the opening goal.

His pass fed Semenyo sprinting down the right and his cross was hung up perfectly for Haaland to head home at the back post.

The Norwegian was denied a second by Carl Rushworth before half-time, but City failed to build on their advantage and were left clinging on for the three points.

Donnarumma was needed to produce two huge saves to deny Loum Tchaouna and Ellis Simms an equaliser and a historic moment for Coventry.

Yet, despite another defeat, there was plenty of encouragement for Lampard that Coventry can compete back in the big time after daunting trips to Arsenal and City in their opening three games.

"What we can't do is lose belief," said the former England midfielder.

"We've got to take confidence from today and look forward and understand that they''ve been two very tough games. But today we can walk out of here with our heads held very high and we need to take that forward to Brighton next week."

Maresca will know City will need to be much improved when they travel to local rivals Manchester United next weekend.

But City do move to the top of the table ahead of champions Arsenal''s clash against Chelsea on Sunday.

item.title: President revokes penalties against 20 NBR officials
item.description:
President Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir has revoked disciplinary penalties imposed on 20 National Board of Revenue (NBR) officials for taking part in protests against reforms at the tax authority.
He has accepted their appeals for clemency and ordered the cancellation of the penalties. The Internal Resources Division (IRD) has issued separate notifications to this effect for each official.
The officials were transferred to different posts during protests by NBR officials and employees in June 2025 against reforms in the revenue sector. Some publicly tore up their transfer orders, while others played key roles in organising the movement and joined the protests by suspending operations at their respective offices.
Departmental proceedings were initiated against them for allegedly violating Rule 30A of the Government Servants (Conduct) Rules, 1979, and relevant provisions of the Government Servants (Discipline and Appeal) Rules, 2018.
After the allegations were established, they were given various punishments, including suspension for different periods and demotion in pay grade.
Those whose penalties have been revoked include Commissioner (currently in charge) Zakir Hossain; Additional Tax Commissioners Hasan Tariq Rikabdar, Mirza Ashik Rana, Chand Sultana Chowdhurani, Sultana Habib, Murad Ahmed, Sifat-e-Marion, A A Amimul Ehsan and Sadhan Kumar Kundu.
Also on the list are Joint Tax Commissioners Monalisa Shahreen, Mamun Mia, Masuma Khatun, Morshed Uddin Khan and Sanowarul Kabir; Deputy Tax Commissioners Zillur Rahman, Imam Tauhid Hossain, Saidul Islam and Shahadat Jamil; and Revenue Officers Sabuj Mia and Shafiul Bashar.
According to the IRD notifications, the officials sought clemency through appeals against their departmental punishments. After reviewing the appeals, the President accepted them and ordered the penalties revoked.
How the movement began
NBR officials and employees launched the movement after the Revenue Policy and Revenue Management Ordinance was issued on May 12, 2025, opposing the proposed reforms. The movement continued for nearly one and a half months and intensified towards the end of June.
Work stoppages at customs and tax offices during the final days of the fiscal year virtually disrupted revenue collection. Operations remained suspended for several consecutive days at NBR headquarters in Dhaka and customs and tax offices across the country. The protesters also held sit-ins, rallies and demonstrations.
The unprecedented movement in NBR history raised concerns over revenue collection at the end of the fiscal year. The officials and employees eventually suspended the protests following mediation by business leaders.
Authorities later took disciplinary measures against officials who had participated in the movement, including transfers and suspensions. Following departmental investigations, some were suspended while others were demoted in pay grade.
After a lengthy process, the penalties against all 20 officials have now been revoked by presidential order.

item.title: PM urges collective action for pollution-free rivers, liveable environment
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman on Sunday urged everyone to play a responsible role from their respective positions to ensure pollution-free rivers and a clean, liveable environment for future generations.
“We must try to ensure pollution-free rivers and a liveable environment not only for ourselves but also for future generations,” he said.
The Prime Minister made the call at a review meeting on pollution control, waste removal, conservation and management of rivers around Dhaka, ensuring navigability and improving the circular waterways, said a release issued by the PM’s Press Wing.
The meeting was held at the Bangladesh Secretariat in the morning. Tarique Rahman stressed that people should not simply wait for government directives but should also act out of a sense of personal responsibility to protect the environment, rivers and waterways.
The meeting reviewed the overall activities concerning pollution control and waste removal from the Buriganga, Turag, Dhaleshwari, Balu and Shitalakhya rivers and adjacent canals and drains.
Those who attended the meeting also discussed measures to ensure navigability and the natural flow of water in the rivers and improve the existing circular waterways around Dhaka.
The prime minister directed the authorities to take effective steps to quickly implement the plans already undertaken.
He also stressed ensuring proper coordination among the ministries, divisions and agencies concerned to expedite the activities.
Local Government, Rural Development and Co-operatives Minister Dr Abdul Moyeen Khan, Environment, Forest and Climate Change Minister Abdul Awal Mintoo, Industries and Commerce Minister Khandakar Abdul Muktadir, Water Resources Minister Shahiduddin Chowdhury Anee, Shipping Minister Shaikh Rabiul Alam, State Minister for LGRD and Co-operatives Mir Shahe Alam, State Minister for Planning Zonayed Abdur Rahim Saki, State Minister for Shipping Md Razib Ahsan, State Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change Shaikh Faridul Islam and Prime Minister’s Special Assistant Dr Saimum Parvez, among others, attended the meeting.
Prime Minister’s Principal Secretary ABM Abdus Sattar, Commander Dhaka Naval Area Rear Admiral Abdullah-Al-Maksus, secretaries of the relevant ministries and divisions, administrators of Dhaka, Narayanganj and Gazipur city corporations and other senior officials were also present.

Body of Bangladeshi killed in Lebanon drone strike reaches Satkhira
item.description:
The body of a Bangladeshi worker from Kalaroa upazila of Satkhira, who was killed in a reported Israeli drone strike in Lebanon, reached his village home on Sunday morning, plunging his family and neighbours into grief.
The deceased was identified as Shuvo Das of Shripatipur village in the upazila.
His body reached home around 10am, about three months and 25 days after his death in a drone strike in a conflict zone in southern Lebanon on May 11.
Shuvo was the second of four siblings, including three brothers and a sister.
His family said he went to Lebanon about two and a half years ago after selling two decimals of their homestead land to meet the cost of migration. He has now returned home in a coffin, leaving his family devastated.
He will be cremated at a local cremation ground after noon.
Shafiqul Islam, 43, of Purbapara village in Sadar upazila, and Nahidul Islam, 22, of Kadakathi village in Ashashuni upazila, of Satkhira were also killed in the Israeli drone strike.
Their bodies reached their respective villages on June 7.
Moin Uddin, a counsellor at the Khulna divisional office of the Ministry of Expatriates’ Welfare and Overseas Employment, said the government provided the family with a cheque for Tk85,000 on Saturday night.
He said the family will receive another Tk3 lakh this month and additional Tk10 lakh from life insurance after a few months.

item.title: 8 arrested over Tk38 lakh robbery in Dhanmondi
item.description:
Police have arrested eight alleged members of a robbery gang in connection with the armed robbery of Tk38 lakh in Dhanmondi, Dhaka.
Deputy Commissioner of the DMP Media and Public Relations Division Md Akter Hossain confirmed the arrests on Sunday.
The arrested individuals are Tanvir Abedin alias Jui, 41; Md Mojibur Rahman, 60; Md Zakir Hossain alias Captain Zakir, 60; Md Solaiman Mridha, 55; Mohammad Kabir Hossain, 50; Abul Kalam Azad, 50; Md Zakaria Hossain alias Lenin, 40; and Sajal Chowdhury, 31.
According to Dhanmondi police, a group of 8-10 people robbed Md Khorshed Alam, 50, of Tk38 lakh at gunpoint around 2:10pm on August 30, 2026.
The robbery took place on the paved road in front of Dingi Restaurant on Road 12/A under Dhanmondi Model police station.
As the robbers fled with the money, Tanvir Abedin and Mojibur Rahman were arrested with the help of police and local residents. A locally made revolver and four rounds of ammunition were recovered from their possession.
Based on information provided by Mojibur Rahman, police later conducted an operation in the Dakshinkhan police station area and arrested Zakir Hossain alias Captain Zakir.
Police subsequently used information provided by the arrested suspects and information technology to conduct raids in different parts of the country, arresting five more alleged members of the gang — Solaiman Mridha, Mohammad Kabir Hossain, Abul Kalam Azad, Zakaria Hossain alias Lenin and Sajal Chowdhury.
During the operations, police recovered Tk345,350 from Zakaria Hossain alias Lenin and Tk230,000 from Sajal Chowdhury.
A total of Tk575,350 of the looted money was recovered and seized.
Police said operations are underway to arrest the remaining absconding and unidentified members of the gang and recover the rest of the stolen money.
A robbery case and a separate case under the Arms Act have been filed with Dhanmondi Model police station in connection with the incident.

item.title: High Court grants Bidisha bail in fraud case, no bar to release
item.description:
The High Court has granted bail to Bidisha Siddique, former wife of late president and Jatiya Party founding chairman Hussain Muhammad Ershad, in a fraud case, clearing the way for her release, lawyers said.
A High Court bench comprising Justice Md Khairul Alam and Justice Md Rafizul Islam passed the order on Sunday.
Earlier, on May 20, a Dhaka metropolitan magistrate’s court sentenced Bidisha to two years’ rigorous imprisonment in the case filed over the sale of a flat.
Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Jamshed Alam also fined her Tk10,000, with one month’s imprisonment in default. The court issued a warrant for her arrest after she was absent when the verdict was announced.
On August 26, Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Aminul Islam Junaid ordered Bidisha to be sent to jail following a hearing in the case.
The case was filed on February 7, 2008, by businessman Mosharraf Hossain.
According to the complaint, Mosharraf, an importer and sanitary products businessman based in Mirpur-10, contacted Bidisha in 2001 to purchase a flat.
The complaint said they later reached an agreement for the sale of a flat at President Park in Baridhara for Tk80 lakh.

item.title: Salahuddin: Global support crucial for sustainable Rohingya solution
item.description:
Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed on Sunday said a quick and sustainable political solution to the Rohingya crisis requires strong cooperation from the international community and international organizations.
He urged the UN and the international community to keep the Rohingya crisis on the global agenda and ensure that it is not overshadowed by other global conflicts or crises.
“Through joint efforts and effective diplomacy by the international community, we must ensure the rapid and dignified repatriation of Rohingya refugees to their homeland in Myanmar,” the minister said while addressing a round-table discussion titled “The Rohingya Crisis: Emerging Challenges & Reframing Response Strategies.”
The Institute for Global Cooperation Foundation (IGCF) organized the program at the auditorium of the Bangladesh Institute of International and Strategic Studies (BIISS).
Salahuddin said a permanent and sustainable solution to the crisis is possible with the direct support of leading countries in global politics and the UN.
He urged international human rights organizations, the UN high commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) and all other relevant stakeholders to play a more effective role in resolving the Rohingya crisis.
“Our main goal is one – to ensure that the nearly 1.5 million Forcibly Displaced Myanmar Nationals (FDMNs) currently taking shelter here can be sent back to their own country with full dignity and security,” the minister said.
“For this, continued support from the international community and the political role of leading countries are extremely important,” he said.
Highlighting the long-term impact of the crisis, Salahuddin said Bangladesh has been providing shelter, food, land, healthcare and basic security for livelihood to more than 1.5 million displaced Rohingyas on humanitarian grounds for over nine years.
“But over time, criminal activities, arms and drug smuggling, human trafficking, gender-based violence and activities of armed groups have increased in the camps, creating serious challenges to Bangladesh’s internal security,” he said.
Noting that the lives and environment of local communities living near the camps have also come under serious threat, the minister said necessary security measures such as fencing around the camps and a well-regulated movement system have become essential to control crime and ensure the overall security of both the Rohingya population and local citizens.
“The present government, under the capable and far-sighted leadership of Prime Minister Tarique Rahman, is determined to implement a 100% successful repatriation,” he said.
A “National Strategy Formulation Committee on Rohingya Affairs” has already been formed under the dynamic leadership of Prime Minister Tarique Rahman, Salahuddin said, adding that another high-level national committee, headed by himself, is active in maintaining law and order, border management and overall coordination.
“The government is working with a comprehensive whole-of-government approach involving the civil administration, security and defence agencies,” he said.
The minister warned that humanitarian assistance provided indefinitely without a specific and credible repatriation plan could reduce the pressure for a political solution in the long run.
“Therefore, going beyond emergency relief assistance, we need to move quickly towards a "transitional strategy", whose main objective will be to create a safe and suitable environment in Myanmar’s Rakhine State for the Rohingyas to return,” he said.
Salahuddin expressed hope that through a combination of sustainable international engagement, national unity and a strong security framework, Bangladesh will soon be able to ensure the dignified and permanent repatriation of Rohingyas to their homeland.
Prime Minister’s Adviser on Public Administration Md Ismail Zabihullah delivered a speech as the guest of honour, while State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaed Islam attended the program as a special guest.

item.title: Buet student Sunny murder: Case report postponed for 43rd time
item.description:
A Dhaka court has postponed the submission of the investigation report in the murder case of Bangladesh University of Engineering and Technology (Buet) student Tarikuzzaman Sunny to October 6, marking the 43rd delay in submitting the report.
The report was scheduled to be submitted on Sunday. However, the investigation officer, SI Mashiur Rahman of Qutubpur Naval Police Outpost, failed to submit it. Following a petition seeking more time, Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate of Dhaka Mahbubur Rahman set October 6 as the new date.
SI of the Prosecution Department Mazharul Islam confirmed the matter.
On the afternoon of July 14, 2022, Tarikuzzaman Sunny, a fifth-year student of the Department of Architecture at Buet, went missing while visiting Moinat Ghat in Dohar with 15 friends.
Sunny, son of Harun Or Rashid, was a resident of Hazaribagh in Dhaka.
After he went missing, a diving team from the Fire Service and Civil Defence headquarters conducted a search. Despite extensive efforts that night, he could not be found. His body was recovered from Moinat Ghat at around 11:26am on July 15.
Sunny’s elder brother Hasanuzzaman filed a murder case that afternoon, accusing the 15 friends who had been with him at the ghat.
The accused were arrested after the case was filed and are currently out on bail.
They are Shariful Hossain, Shakil Ahmed, Sejan Ahmed, Rubel, Sajeeb, Nurzaman, Nasir, Maruf, Ashraful Alam, Jahangir Hossain Liton, Noman, Zahid, ATM Shahriar Momin, Maruful Haque Maruf and Roknuzzaman alias Jitu.

item.title: Humaiun Kobir lauds Japan’s efforts for durable Rohingya solution
item.description:
State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir on Sunday appreciated Japan's efforts toward achieving a durable solution through the safe, voluntary, sustainable, and dignified repatriation of the Rohingyas to Rakhine State in Myanmar.
He also appreciated the Nippon Foundation and Japan's humanitarian assistance for the forcibly displaced Myanmar nationals.
The state minister said Bangladesh remains firmly committed to working with the international community to resolve this prolonged humanitarian and regional challenge.
He made the remarks when Honorary Chair of the Nippon Foundation of Japan Yohei Sasakawa paid a courtesy call on him at his office.
During the meeting, Yohei Sasakawa mentioned that the relationship between the Nippon Foundation and the People's Republic of Bangladesh is built upon a history of profound friendship and mutual trust that spans over half a century, said the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.
“Our cooperative efforts began in 1971 with emergency relief for displaced persons during your nation's independence,” he said.
"Since then, we have consistently stood by the people of Bangladesh, supporting various developmental, healthcare, and educational initiatives. In recent years, our attention has been heavily dedicated to the Rohingya humanitarian crisis," Sasakawa noted.
He informed the State Minister that for over 40 years, he and his organisation have been closely involved in efforts to eliminate leprosy, working in close cooperation with the World Health Organization (WHO), governments, international organizations and NGOs, and organizations of persons affected by leprosy.
They wish to assist leprosy patients in Bangladesh.

item.title: Rangpur shrine caretaker murder: Death sentences upheld for 2, 5 acquitted
item.description:
The High Court on Sunday acquitted five people and upheld the death sentences of two others in the murder case of Rangpur shrine caretaker Rahmat Ali, 60.
The death sentences of JMB commander Masud Rana and Liton Mia were upheld.
The five acquitted by the High Court are JMB members Ishaq Ali, 34; Sakhawat Hossain alias Rahul, 30; Sarwar Hossain Sabu alias Mizan, 30; northern region commander Bijoy alias Ali alias Dorji, 30; and Chandu Mia, 20.
The High Court bench of Justice Zafar Ahmed and Justice Sathika Hossain delivered the verdict on Sunday.
Advocate SM Shahjahan and Barrister Anwar Hossain represented the accused before the court.
In 2018, a Rangpur court sentenced seven accused to death and acquitted six others in the case. Rangpur Special Judge Naresh Chandra Sarkar delivered the verdict.
The seven sentenced to death were JMB's Rangpur region commander Masud Rana alias Mamun alias Montri, 33; Ishaq Ali, 34; Liton Mia alias Rafiq, 32; Sakhawat Hossain alias Rahul, 30; Sarwar Hossain Sabu alias Mizan, 30; northern region commander Bijoy alias Ali alias Dorji, 30; and Chandu Mia, 20.
The six acquitted by the trial court were JMB members Abu Sayeed, 30; Toufiqul Islam Sabuj, 35; Sadat alias Ratan Mia, 23; Jahangir Hossain alias Rajib Gandhi, 26; Babul Akhtar alias Babul Master, 35; and Rajibul Islam Molla alias Badal alias Badhan, 25.
Two of the 13 accused, Chandu Mia and Rajibul Islam Molla alias Badal alias Badhan, were absconding.
Rahmat Ali, the caretaker of a shrine, was hacked indiscriminately and had his throat slit at Chaitar Mor in Madhupur union of Kaunia upazila, Rangpur, while returning home on the night of November 10, 2015.
The following day, his son Shafiqul Islam filed a murder case with Kaunia Police Station.

item.title: The iPad didn't fail. We just asked the wrong question
item.description:
Apple turns fifty this year. The iPhone rewired human connectivity. The Mac defined the personal workstation.
But the product that most accurately captures Apple's instincts—its hardware ambition, its ecosystem ruthlessness, and its particular genius for building exactly the right thing while arguing about something else entirely—is the iPad.
And we have spent sixteen years prosecuting the wrong argument about it.
Here is what the right argument looks like: On my desk right now sits an M4 Mac mini.
It is a utilitarian workhorse that handles the heavy lifting, the cognitive load of my professional life. But when I step away from that desk, I do not reach for a laptop. I reach for my iPad Air.
That split, almost instinctive, is the entire thesis.
The chair was the point
When Steve Jobs unveiled the iPad on January 27, 2010, he did not stand at a podium. He did not sit at a desk. He sank into a leather armchair casually with a device resting in his lap.
In retrospect, we should have read that as a design brief. He was showing us exactly where this thing was supposed to live – in the space between the phone in your pocket and the computer at your desk.
The industry missed it completely. Apple sold 300,000 units on launch day and 15 million in the first year, outpacing the iPhone's early adoption curve.
And yet the dominant critical response was “giant iPod Touch.” For the next decade, reviewers held the iPad against a MacBook and declared it a failure for not being one. It was like reviewing a bicycle for not being a car.
What actually happened
While enthusiasts debated file system access and terminal windows, the iPad was quietly rewriting entire industries, not because it was trying to replace anything, but precisely because it was not.
In 2011, US commercial aviation authorized the iPad to replace 40-pound paper flight bags in cockpits.
Airlines saved millions in fuel costs annually. That decision was not made because the iPad ran professional software suites.
It was made because it was light, reliable, and instantly operable by people who needed to fly planes, not configure operating systems.
In healthcare, 75% of US physicians integrated iPad devices into clinical rounds within a few years of its launch.
Not because of raw processing power. Because a tablet is the right form factor for a hospital ward. It can be handed to a patient, held with one arm, sanitized between rooms.
When Covid-19 hit, Stanford Healthcare deployed iPads into patient rooms in just eight days.
Every deployment reduced the number of times a healthcare worker physically entered a room. It saved PPE. For isolated patients, that screen was the only way to see their families.
No laptop accomplished that. No phone would have been adequate.
The iPad did not fail to become a Mac. It succeeded at something a Mac was never built to do.
The contradiction Apple created
This is where the traditional narrative gets intellectually lazy: blaming the audience for “mis-categorizing” the iPad while ignoring that Apple sent every possible mixed signal for fifteen years.
Apple released the Magic Keyboard. Apple ran the “What's a computer?” campaign. Apple priced the iPad Pro directly against MacBook Airs.
Apple introduced Stage Manager, a feature that only makes sense if you are trying to do laptop tasks on a tablet.
Tim Cook told shareholders the iPad Pro could replace someone's primary computer.
Apple built the entire keyboard case accessory ecosystem around a product it insists is not a laptop.
You cannot market a device as a laptop replacement, price it like one, build peripherals for it like one, and then argue the audience was confused.
That is not a consumer problem. That is an identity crisis Apple deliberately cultivated because the iPad Pro needed a premium positioning story.
The confusion was manufactured. The real story was quieter and far more interesting.
The 30% wall
The conventional explanation for why the iPad was never given full Mac capabilities was that Apple was protecting Mac hardware sales.
That argument was always structurally weak.
If hardware protection was the goal, Apple would not have put the M-series silicon in the iPad at all. The real reason is the App Store.
Every software freedom Apple grants the iPad — true sideloading, full desktop-class application installation from the open web–is a direct cut to one of Apple's highest-margin revenue streams.
The App Store's commission structure, which takes up to 30% on digital transactions, is the anchor of Apple's Service division, a segment that generates $109.1 billion in 2025 (out of a total company revenue of $416.1 billion).
Furthermore, the App store facilitated a staggering $1.4 trillion in developer billings and sales that year.
The iPad was not capped by hardware limitations. It was capped by ecosystem economics.
The M-series chips proved the point with crystal clarity.
The M5 iPad Pro has more raw processing power than most desktop rigs on the market. For years, it could not manage a simple file folder with real intuition.
It could render 4K footage but struggled with window management. Apple built a computational Ferrari and installed a software limiter on the throttle not to protect the Mac, but to protect the 30% cut.
That dynamic is finally shifting. iPadOS 26 is the clearest signal, yet that Apple is willing to let the software approach the silicon.
But even as that gap closes, the structural tension remains: Apple will allow the iPad to be free enough to justify its price, but never free enough to threaten the ecosystem that funds it.
The reversal nobody saw coming
The most important inflection point in the iPad's history was not a chip. It was a stylus, and it required Apple to publicly contradict its own founder.
In 2007, Steve Jobs dismissed the stylus with memorable contempt: " Yuck. Nobody wants a stylus ."
But eight years later, Tim Cook built an entire product identity around one.
On September 9, 2015, Apple introduced the iPad Pro alongside the Apple Pencil and quietly shifted the iPad's narrative from consumption to creation.
Before 2015, serious digital illustration required a desktop machine, a Wacom tablet, and software that cost hundreds of dollars annually.
The Pencil and a $13 app called Procreate dismantled that infrastructure entirely. Legendary artists like David Hockney transitioned from canvas to iPad and sold digital works for millions.
Musicians, architects, journalists, and cinematographers followed.
The creative reversal was real, and it was the iPad's most honest pitch to date. Not “I can replace your laptop.” But “I can do things your laptop cannot.”
What iPadOS 26 actually means
The M5 iPad Pro arriving alongside iPadOS 26 is the most significant moment in the iPad's post-2015 history.
Applications are beginning to operate with genuine desktop-class depth. File management is becoming less theatrical.
The gap between what the silicon can execute and what the software permits is, finally, narrowing in a meaningful way.
But this does not kill the companion thesis. It refines it.
The iPad is not becoming a Mac. If that were the goal, Apple would have shipped macOS on an iPad years ago.
What is actually happening is more precise: the iPad is becoming the fullest version of what it always was.
A more capable companion is still a companion. Better software doesn't change the form factor.
It does not change where the device lives. It does not change what you reach for when you leave your desk.
It just makes the iPad better at being the iPad.
The dream was always about the carrying
In 1983, long before the Mac had fully matured, Steve Jobs told an audience he wanted to build “an incredibly great computer in a book that you can carry around with you, that you can learn how to use in twenty minutes.”
Jobs did not say a computer to carry around instead of your workstation.
He said a computer in a book that you carry around with you. The carrying was not incidental. The carrying was the product.
Forty-three years later, that is exactly what the iPad is. Not the machine you work at.
The machine you work with in the places your desktop cannot follow. The couch. The cockpit. The hospital room. The corner of a creative studio at three in the morning. Light enough to take everywhere. Powerful enough to matter when you need.
iPad turns sweet 16
The iPad is not the best computer. It is not the best phone. It will not replace either. It is the only device that occupies the in-between with any real authority.
The only screen that can be a reading pane, a creative canvas, a clinical tool, a cockpit instrument, and a lifeline for a patient who cannot leave their room—all without pretending to be something it is not.
We spent 16 years demanding it become a laptop. We were asking the wrong question.
The right question was always simpler: what does the space between your phone and your computer actually need?
The iPad answered that question from a leather armchair in 2010. We just looked but did not see.
Happy 16th birthday, iPad. You were right all along.
The writer is a contributor and tech enthusiast

item.title: Sophos: Identity-based attacks responsible for 85% ransomware in education
item.description:
Sophos, a global cybersecurity leader, recently released its annual State of Ransomware in Education 2026 Sophos State of Ransomware in Education report, which found that identity-based attack techniques were used in 85% of ransomware attacks against education institutions.
Those techniques include malicious email, phishing, compromised credentials and brute force attacks.
The 85% rate exceeded the cross-sector average of 79%, underscoring the role identity compromise continues to play in ransomware incidents targeting lower and higher education institutions.
Malicious email was the leading technical root cause of ransomware attacks in both lower education (31%) and higher education (29%).
The report also found that 77% of higher education organizations and 71% of lower education organizations said their ransomware incident was also their most significant identity attack.
Education institutions also recover more slowly from attacks.
Lower and higher education institutions are roughly twice as likely as the cross-sector average to need one to three months to fully recover.
Lower education fared worst of all: 31% took a month or more to get back on their feet, the highest share of any sector.
Sophos CISO Ross McKerchar said: “Educational institutions are prime targets because they hold large amounts of personal data but have limited resources. He warned that identity theft and AI are making cyberattacks faster and more sophisticated, urging institutions to strengthen identity security and threat detection.”
The report also highlights several key findings about cybersecurity challenges in the education sector.
The findings are based on an independent survey of 226 IT and cybersecurity leaders across 17 countries, conducted between January and March 2026.
This is the sixth year Sophos has tracked ransomware trends in education.

item.title: NCC Bank donates Tk1cr to Dhaka Community Hospital
item.description:
Under its CSR program, NCC Bank has donated Tk1 crore to Dhaka Community Hospital (DCH) for the purchase of a state-of-the-art CT scan machine.
This initiative will expedite diagnosis and treatment, particularly for trauma, stroke, emergency, and cancer patients, while also expanding access to affordable healthcare.
This 500-bed non-profit hospital has long been providing affordable healthcare to low-income and underprivileged communities.
Currently lacking its own high-resolution CT scan facility, the hospital faced certain limitations in patient care.
To address this gap, NCC Bank has provided this financial assistance from its CSR fund.
Recently, at an event held at NCC Bank head office, chairman of the bank Md Nurun Newaz Salim handed over a cheque for Tk1 crore to chairman (acting) of the DCH Trust Quazi Habibur Rahman.
Among others, NCC Bank vice chairman Engineer Abdus Salam, chairman of the executive committee Khairul Alam Chaklader, directors Syed Asif Nizamuddin, Mohammed Sazzad Un Newaz and Morshedul Alam Chaklader, managing director M Shamsul Arefin, additional managing director M Khurshed Alam, deputy managing director Md Habibur Rahman, and company secretary (current charge) Md Nazrul Islam Chowdhury, along with executive & director of DCH Trust Prof Dr Md Omar Sharif Ibne Hasan, members of DCH Trust Sukumar Chakrabortty, Md Jabed Yousuf, Md Wakar Hossain, assistant director Dr Md Fuadul Islam, and member Md Ariful Islam were present.
NCC Bank chairman Md Nurun Newaz Salim said: "Ensuring affordable and accessible healthcare is an essential part of our commitment to society. The installation of this high-capacity CT scan machine at Dhaka Community Hospital will enable patients to receive rapid diagnosis and treatment, while also alleviating some of the financial burden on them and their families."
The bank's managing director M Shamsul Arefin said: "One of the key objectives of NCC Bank's CSR initiatives is to ensure healthcare for low-income and underprivileged people, especially those suffering from critical illnesses. Today's assistance aims to enhance the diagnostic capabilities of Dhaka Community Hospital and help deliver essential healthcare to more people at an affordable cost."
Quazi Habibur Rhaman, acting chairman of the Dhaka Community Hospital Trust, expressed his gratitude to NCC Bank, saying: "Starting with just 20 beds, Dhaka Community Hospital has now grown into a 500-bed healthcare facility. We remain committed to serving those who cannot afford expensive treatments. This support from NCC Bank will fill a crucial gap in our diagnostic services, enabling us to provide essential CT scan services more efficiently and cost-effectively."

item.title: Community Bank’s Clean Dhaka Project promotes cleanliness and tree plantation
item.description:
With the theme “Amar Shahor, Amar Desh— Poricchonnotay Bodle Zabe Bangladesh,” Community Bank Bangladesh PLC. organized cleanliness and tree plantation programs under its ‘Community Bank Clean Dhaka Project’ with the aim of building a clean, green and livable Bangladesh.
The programs were held on Saturday at Viqarunnisa Noon School & College and Rajarbagh Police Lines School & College in the capital.
Around 500 students and teachers of the two educational institutions, along with officials and employees of Community Bank Bangladesh PLC participated in the programs.
With the active participation of the students, cleanliness drives were conducted on the premises and surrounding areas of the two institutions, while saplings of different species were also planted.
Dhaka South City Corporation Administrator Md Abdus Salam; Inspector General of Police, Bangladesh and chairman of Community Bank Bangladesh PLC Md Ali Hossain Fakir; Dhaka Metropolitan Police Commissioner Mosleh Uddin Ahmed; and managing director of Community Bank Bangladesh PLC Mohammed Emtiaz Uddin, along with senior officials of Bangladesh Police, directors of Community Bank, principals of the two educational institutions and other distinguished guests, attended the programs.
Speaking at the event, Inspector General of Police, Bangladesh and chairman of Community Bank Bangladesh PLC Md Ali Hossain Fakir stressed the active role of the younger generation in cleanliness, greenery, tree plantation, personal awareness, drug prevention and maintaining law and order.
“Cleanliness and greenery are among the key prerequisites for a beautiful and livable city. It is not enough to keep roads, streets and our surroundings clean; we must plant more trees to make our cities greener and take care of every tree we plant. A tree not only helps maintain environmental balance, but also ensures clean air, shade and a better environment for future generations,” he said.
Dhaka South City Corporation administrator Md Abdus Salam said: “Nature is behaving adversely because the balance of nature has been disrupted. There is no alternative to planting trees if we want to protect our country and nature.”
Dhaka Metropolitan Police Commissioner Mosleh Uddin Ahmed said: “A collective effort is needed to build a clean Dhaka. It is extremely important to engage the younger generation in such social activities.”
Mohammed Emtiaz Uddin, managing director of Community Bank Bangladesh PLC, emphasized the need to initiate change from within oneself.
As part of efforts to sustain cleanliness practices, 20 dustbins, 20 shovels and 20 brooms were provided to each of the two educational institutions. In addition, 12 fruit-bearing, timber, medicinal and flowering trees were planted at each institution.

item.title: bKash, Bishwo Shahitto Kendro celebrate 12 years of joint journey in book reading program
item.description:
“What a person observes in childhood, they try to recreate it throughout their life,” said Prof Abdullah Abu Sayeed, chairman and chief executive of Bishwo Shahitto Kendro.
The eminent educator and writer reminisced about how deeply his father influenced him in spreading books and the habit of reading.
Regarding the expansion of the book reading program across the country, he said: “There were many struggles along this journey, but we also received help from many quarters- personal, social, institutional, and government support. Among the non-state organizations that provided major assistance, one was bKash.”
“Over these 12 years, we received 400,000 books from bKash, which were distributed to various educational institutions nationwide. These 400,000 books have been read by at least 3.2 million readers and students. If bKash had invested this money elsewhere, they might have made a profit. Whether bKash benefited financially from it or not, I don’t know, but the nation has certainly benefited from the partnership,” he added.
Prof Sayeed expressed these views in a video message during an event organized in the capital on Friday (September 4) to mark the 12th anniversary of the partnership between Bishwo Shahitto Kendra and bKash to spread the book reading program across the country.
Dr ANM Ehsanul Hoque Milon, Minister of Education, attended the event as chief guest.
Among others present were Kamal Quadir, chief executive officer of bKash; Major General Sheikh Md Monirul Islam (retd), chief external and corporate affairs officer of bKash; and Khandakar Md Asaduzzaman, executive director of Bishwo Shahitto Kendro.
Additionally, over three hundred students and their teachers from various schools as well as civil society members attended the event.
In his chief guest’s address, Education Minister stated: “Positive change is needed in society, and the Prime Minister is working hard toward it. The government is giving the highest priority to improving the quality of education in the country, which must begin right from the primary level. Priority is also being given to technical education.”
bKash’s founder and CEO Kamal Quadir said: “Since the beginning of our journey, bKash’s goal has been to bring a positive change in the economy by driving financial inclusion in the country. At the same time, as a responsible corporate entity, we believe that education and the pursuit of knowledge are among the core foundations of sustainable development. It is from this belief that bKash has been associated with Bishwo Shahitto Kendro’s book reading program for the last 12 years.”
The nationwide ‘Book Reading Program’ of Bishwo Shahitto Kendro stands as one of the largest and long-term initiatives dedicated to instilling reading habits, critical thinking, and human values among students.
For over four decades, Bishwo Shahitto Kendro has been running this program across the country.
Embracing this vision of Bishwo Shahitto Kendro as part of its corporate social responsibility, bKash has been continuously associated with the initiative for 12 years since 2014.
Through this partnership, bKash has distributed more than 400,000 books to libraries of various educational institutions across the country.
The books distributed have reached nearly 3,000 educational institutions, directly benefiting over 3.2 million students and readers.

item.title: BKMEA: Withdraw ban on knit fabric import
item.description:
The Bangladesh Knitwear Manufacturers and Exporters Association (BKMEA) has urged the government to immediately withdraw a provision in the new import policy for 2026-29 that prohibits the import of knit fabrics.
In a letter to the commerce minister on September 2, BKMEA President Mohammad Hatem expressed concern over sub-clause 12 of provision 25 of the policy, which states that "knit fabrics shall not be importable."
According to the letter, authorities had acknowledged during previous consultations with industry stakeholders that the restrictive provision was included inadvertently and assured the industry that it would be removed.
However, the restriction remained in the official gazette published by the commerce ministry on August 24, 2026.
The BKMEA chief highlighted that the ongoing gas crisis has severely disrupted domestic textile mills and fabric production.
As such, local manufacturers are unable to meet the volume, specialized technical standards and design variations required by international buyers, making raw materials import unavoidable.
The association also noted that several garment exporters had opened letters of credit for raw knit fabrics before the gazette was published.
Many of those shipments have already arrived at Chittagong Port or are in transit, according to the letter.
BKMEA warned that enforcing the ban would prevent customs clearance, causing shipment delays, financial losses and potential cancellation of export orders.
It urged the government to immediately suspend or repeal the provision to ensure uninterrupted production and fulfillment of buyers' commitments.

item.title: 14 Boeing aircraft: Buying more than planes
item.description:
Biman Bangladesh Airlines is set to acquire 14 new Boeing aircraft. At around $3.7 billion, the decision has naturally attracted debate. Some question whether Bangladesh, given its present economic pressures, should make an investment of this size. Others see it largely through a political lens, with criticism extending to the government itself.

But to look at the purchase only in terms of its immediate cost would miss the larger question: where does Bangladesh want to see its national airline 20 years from now?

We often speak of Emirates and Qatar Airways. Dubai and Doha did not become global aviation hubs simply by building modern airports. Their success came through years of investment in aircraft, routes and connectivity, eventually creating a business that carries passengers not only to their home countries but through them to the rest of the world.

Bangladesh is different, and the comparison should not be taken too far. But there is a lesson here. Aviation is a long-term business. Investments made today may be intended for markets that will take a decade or more to develop.

Seen from that perspective, Biman’s plan deserves a more considered assessment. The proposed fleet includes eight Boeing 787-10s, two 787-9s and four 737-8s, intended for a combination of Middle Eastern, regional and long-haul routes. Deliveries are expected to begin towards the end of 2031 and continue until 2035.

The timeline matters. Bangladesh is making a decision today about the aviation market it expects to compete in during the 2030s and beyond.
There is also an economic argument for acting early. No one can say with certainty what comparable aircraft will cost five years from now. Inflation, production costs, technology, supply chains and long delivery cycles all influence aircraft prices.

If similar aircraft were to cost even 20 or 30 percent more in five years, securing commercial terms and production slots earlier could itself provide a significant procurement advantage. This does not mean such an increase is certain. It simply means that the cost of waiting should also be part of the calculation.

Biman’s financial position is relevant too. In FY2024-25, the airline reported Tk 11,559 crore in revenue, Tk 1,602 crore in operating profit and more than Tk 785 crore in net profit. It carried around 3.4 million passengers and earned Tk 925 crore from cargo. A company that has remained profitable for five consecutive years must eventually decide whether to maintain its present position or invest in expansion.

Operationally, there is another advantage. Biman already flies Boeing 787s and 737s. Existing experience in pilot training, engineering, maintenance and spare-parts management can therefore support the expanded fleet. Improved fuel efficiency could also produce substantial savings over an aircraft’s operating life.

The purchase also sits within the wider Bangladesh-US commercial relationship. The proposed Boeing acquisition is connected to a broader trade framework involving market access and other economic commitments. To view it only through Biman’s balance sheet would therefore leave out part of the picture.

None of this means the deal should escape scrutiny. A multibillion-dollar investment demands transparency. The final negotiated price, financing cost, repayment period, route strategy and expected aircraft utilisation should all be clear. If sovereign guarantees are involved, accountability becomes even more important.

Fleet expansion is fine, but its success will depend on what happens after the aircraft arrive. Buying planes alone will not turn Biman into Emirates or Qatar Airways. The harder task will be keeping them in the air, filling their seats, carrying profitable cargo, opening the right routes and gradually making Dhaka a competitive connecting point.

Bangladesh cannot aspire to build a serious international airline while planning only a few years ahead.

Ultimately, the debate should not end with the $3.7 billion price tag. The real question is whether Bangladesh can turn these 14 aircraft into a profitable aviation business for the next 20 years.

item.title: Fertiliser dealer’s warehouse vandalised in Kurigram, roadblock in Lalmonirhat
item.description:
Angry farmers vandalised a fertiliser dealer’s warehouse at Kachakata Bazar in Nageshwari upazila of Kurigram, after the distribution of fertiliser was delayed.

Farmers also staged a road blockade in Bhurungamari upazila of the district demanding fertiliser. In Lalmonirhat, farmers likewise blocked a road and staged demonstrations over the same demand.

Local farmers said they began gathering outside Kashem Traders, a fertiliser dealer at Kachakata Bazar in Nageshwari, from 7:00 am to collect fertiliser. As the dealer’s representatives had still not arrived after 8:00 am, frustration grew among the farmers waiting there. At one point, around 200 farmers had gathered. At about 9:00 am, the farmers began shouting and protesting. Several of them then vandalised part of the warehouse’s corrugated-tin fencing. However, local farmers said no fertiliser was taken from the warehouse as others intervened.

Several farmers said tensions escalated because the dealer’s representatives failed to arrive for a long time despite fertiliser being available at the warehouse. Pushing and jostling broke out among the farmers, after which some of them damaged the corrugated-tin fencing.

Arpan Kumar Das, officer-in-charge of Kachakata police station, told Prothom Alo that the dealer had sufficient fertiliser in the warehouse.

He said the farmers became angry because the dealer arrived somewhat late. During pushing and jostling among 150 to 200 people, sections of the warehouse’s corrugated-tin fencing were damaged.

Police later arrived, brought the situation under control and distributed the fertiliser. The situation is now normal, he added.

Meanwhile, farmers blocked a road at Milan Bazar in Baladia Union of Bhurungamari after failing to obtain fertiliser. Traffic on the road was halted for some time. Police went to the scene after being informed.

Later, Upazila Assistant Commissioner (Land) Aminul Haque Tareque arrived at the scene and spoke with the farmers, after which the situation returned to normal.

Aminul Haque Tareque told Prothom Alo that farmers from surrounding areas had gathered after hearing that fertiliser would be distributed from a warehouse at Milan Bazar. This brought traffic on the road to a standstill. The warehouse had 20 tonnes of fertiliser, but distribution was not possible that day because of the large number of farmers.

An additional supply of fertiliser would be brought in the following day and distributed together, he said.

Road blockade in Lalmonirhat

Angry farmers blocked a highway in Lalmonirhat by placing tree trunks on the road, demanding an adequate supply of fertiliser and an end to the alleged “fertiliser syndicate”.

The blockade was staged at around 11:00 am today in the Mahendranagar Bazar area of Lalmonirhat Sadar on the Lalmonirhat–Patgram–Burimari highway. Traffic on the highway remained halted for around an hour.

The protesting farmers later withdrew the blockade following intervention by the district administration and assurances that fertiliser supplies would be ensured.

The protesting farmers alleged that they had been unable to apply fertiliser to their fields on time during the ongoing Aman cultivation season because they had not received adequate supplies according to demand.

They also said they were forced to take to the national highway to demand a regular supply of fertiliser and an end to the artificial shortage or alleged syndicate surrounding its distribution.

Upon receiving the news, Lalmonirhat Deputy Commissioner Md Rashedul Haque Pradhan, Superintendent of Police Md Asaduzzaman, Upazila Nirbahi Officer Mononita Das and local Mahendranagar Union Parishad chairman Md Abdul Majid Mondal quickly arrived at the scene.

They assured the farmers that positive steps would be taken to address their demands, following which the protesters left the road.

Addressing the farmers, Deputy Commissioner Md Rashedul Haque Pradhan said there was essentially no shortage of fertiliser in Lalmonirhat district.

He said a misunderstanding had temporarily arisen after a large number of farmers from Lalmonirhat Sadar gathered at Mahendranagar upon hearing that fertiliser was being distributed in a union in Hatibandha.

He added that if any specific allegation of an artificial fertiliser shortage was received, the authorities would investigate it and take immediate and strict administrative action.
